clauses: The number and types of actions to take during a turn.
Whether actions may be repeated or skipped.
When and where to discard if the hand temporarily contains 9 cards, and the resulting hand size.
answers.answer: Take 2 actions; repeating an action is allowed, but skipping an action is not. A hand of 9 is allowed during the turn; at turn end, discard 2 cards to your own discard pile to reach 7, then the opponent takes their turn.

evidence.text: At the start of Medusa’s turn, her optional special ability may resolve (see below). Then take **2 actions** from **maneuver, scheme, attack**. You may repeat an action, including maneuver twice; **you cannot skip an action**.
You may hold more than 7 cards during your turn. **At the end of your turn**, discard excess cards to your own discard pile until you have **7**, then the opponent takes their turn.

clauses: A mandatory card draw occurs before maneuver movement.

answers.answer: Draw 1 card first. Then optionally move your fighters one at a time, each up to its move value plus applicable bonuses and including a choice of zero; choose their order and finish each fighter’s movement before starting another’s. Movement follows adjacent connecting lines, may pass through friendly fighters, may not pass through opposing fighters, and may not end in any occupied space.

evidence.text:
1. **Draw 1 card first, mandatory.**
2. **Optionally move** each of your fighters, one at a time, up to your move value (plus applicable bonuses). Each fighter chooses its own distance, including **zero**. Choose their order, but finish one fighter’s movement before starting another’s.

Ordinary movement enters adjacent spaces along connecting lines. You may pass through your own friendly fighters, but **cannot finish in any occupied space**. You may **not pass through opposing fighters**. An effect that moves opposing fighters follows the same rules **from their owner’s perspective**. Apply these movement restrictions to card movement unless that card states an exception.

The move value applies to **each** of that player’s fighters during maneuver. Harpies have no health dials; each has 1 health. Other fighters have individual dials. Health cannot increase above the highest number on that fighter’s dial.

clauses: A card from hand may be discarded during a maneuver to add its printed BOOST value to that maneuver’s movement value.
Each of the player’s fighters receives the allowance increase.
The discarded card’s effects are ignored.
A defeated sidekick’s card that cannot be played may still be discarded to BOOST.
answers.answer: During a maneuver, discard 1 hand card and add its printed BOOST value to that maneuver’s movement value; each of your fighters receives that allowance. Ignore the discarded card’s effects. A defeated sidekick’s unusable card may still be discarded to BOOST.

evidence.text: **BOOST movement:** during a maneuver, discard **1 card from your hand** to add its printed **BOOST value** (the small circled number, not its combat value) to the movement value for this maneuver. Each of your fighters receives that allowance. For **any permitted BOOST**, add the discarded card’s BOOST value and **ignore that card’s effects**, whether the BOOST modifies movement or an attack. A card that cannot be played because its fighter is defeated **can still be discarded to BOOST**. Effects may separately permit boosting attacks; boosting is not otherwise a universal option.

clauses: Whether drawing cards is mandatory when an effect requires them.
Whether the discard pile is reshuffled when the deck is empty.
For each unfillable draw, how much damage is applied to which fighters; the effect of two required draws and the immediate game-end condition.
answers.answer: You cannot decline the mandatory draws and do not reshuffle. Each missing card causes each of your fighters to take 2 damage immediately: with two required draws, that is two separate 2-damage events (4 total per fighter that survives both events). If a hero is defeated, the game ends immediately.

evidence.text: - Drawing cards, whether from maneuver or an effect, is **mandatory unless explicitly optional**.

- With an empty deck, your fighters are **exhausted**. Each time you must draw a card you cannot draw, **each of your fighters immediately takes 2 damage instead**. Do **not reshuffle** your discard pile. A mandatory draw of 2 with an empty deck therefore causes two separate 2-damage events to every surviving fighter, unless hero defeat has already ended the game. If only one card remains, draw it and take the exhaustion damage for the next missing draw.

clauses: Any fighter may target an adjacent opponent, even across zone boundaries.
Melee fighters may target only adjacent opponents; ranged fighters may also target any opponent sharing a zone regardless of adjacency or distance.
A zone includes all spaces with the same colored pattern, including disconnected spaces; adjacency and shared zone are distinct tests.
answers.answer: Adjacent opponents are legal targets for both melee and ranged fighters, even across zone boundaries. A melee fighter cannot target a nonadjacent opponent in the same zone. A ranged fighter can target a nonadjacent opponent in the same zone, including a disconnected part of that colored zone.

evidence.text: One fighter per circular space. Spaces connected by a line are **adjacent**. A **zone** consists of all spaces with the same colored pattern, even if separated on the board. A space showing several patterns belongs to all those zones. Adjacency and shared zones are different tests.

1. **Declare** your attacking fighter (active fighter) and the opposing fighter targeted. Any fighter may attack an **adjacent** opponent, even across zone boundaries. **Melee** fighters may attack only adjacent opponents. **Ranged** fighters may also attack any opponent sharing a zone, regardless of distance or adjacency, including another separated part of that zone.

clauses: An attack action is illegal without an attack-capable card in hand or a valid target.
The attacking fighter and opposing target are declared before card selection.
The attacker must use an attack card allowed for that fighter; the defender may decline, or use a legal defense card for the defending fighter; reveal follows both choices simultaneously.
Versatile cards may attack or defend and count as both attack and defense cards for other effects; fighter labels and pure card roles restrict use.
answers.answer: An attack action requires both an attack-capable card in hand and a valid target. First declare the attacking fighter and target. The attacker then plays a legal attack card; the defender may decline or choose a legal defense card for the defending fighter. Reveal simultaneously after both choices. Versatile cards may attack or defend and count as both types for other effects; fighter labels and pure attack/defense roles still govern eligibility.

evidence.text: You cannot take an attack action without an attack-capable card in hand or without a valid target for one of your fighters.

1. **Declare** your attacking fighter (active fighter) and the opposing fighter targeted. Any fighter may attack an **adjacent** opponent, even across zone boundaries. **Melee** fighters may attack only adjacent opponents. **Ranged** fighters may also attack any opponent sharing a zone, regardless of distance or adjacency, including another separated part of that zone.

2. **Choose cards:** attacker plays an attack card face down that the attacking fighter is allowed to use. Defender may decline to play a card; otherwise plays a legal defense card face down for the defending fighter. **Reveal simultaneously** after both choices.

Attack-only cards are red, defense-only blue, and **versatile** cards purple. Versatile cards may attack or defend and **count as both attack and defense cards for other effects**. A fighter-specific card cannot be used by a different fighter; **ANY** permits any of your fighters. A pure defense card cannot initiate an attack; a pure attack card cannot defend.

clauses: The ordered combat resolution sequence through card discard.
How effects with the same timing are prioritized, and whether card effects resolve optionally or mandatorily.
How pending after-combat card effects interact with a defeated fighter and whether other after-combat game effects occur.
Where played cards go.
answers.answer: Resolve: (1) immediately effects; (2) during-combat effects; (3) combat result, damage and health reduction; (4) after-combat card effects; (5) other after-combat game effects; (6) discard all played cards. For effects at the same timing, the defender resolves first. Card effects are mandatory unless they say otherwise and resolve in printed order. A defeated fighter’s played card still resolves its after-combat effects unless the game has already ended. Played cards go to their owners’ face-up discard piles.

evidence.text: 1. Resolve **IMMEDIATELY** card effects.
2. Resolve **DURING COMBAT** card effects.

3. Determine combat result: defender takes attack value minus defense value, to a minimum of zero. If no defense card, take the attack value. Reduce the defending fighter’s health by the damage dealt. Defense does not itself deal return damage.
4. Resolve **AFTER COMBAT card effects**. A defeated fighter’s played card still resolves its after-combat effects **unless the game has already ended**.
5. Resolve other after-combat game effects, such as a hero’s special ability.
6. Finally place all played cards in their respective **face-up discard piles**.

**Whenever effects share a timing, the defender’s effect resolves first.** Card effects are **mandatory unless they say otherwise** (for example “may”); this can harm your own fighters. Complete them in the printed order. A card whose effects are canceled keeps its printed combat value; the canceled effects do not resolve.

clauses: Combat damage from value 4 against defense value 4.
Whether the later 2 effect damage changes the combat winner.
Damage with attack value 4 and no defense card.
answers.answer: Attack damage is max(4 − 4, 0) = 0, so the defender wins combat. The later 2 damage is effect damage and does not change the winner. With no defense card, attack damage is 4.

evidence.text: 3. Determine combat result: defender takes attack value minus defense value, to a minimum of zero. If no defense card, take the attack value. Reduce the defending fighter’s health by the damage dealt. Defense does not itself deal return damage.

**Winning combat is not winning the game:** the attacker wins combat only if the **attack itself** deals at least 1 damage. If it deals none, the **defender wins**, including a tie of values or a defense that prevents the attack damage. Damage from effects does **not** change this winner.

clauses: The result when a sidekick reaches zero and what happens to its token.
Whether its played card’s after-combat effect resolves if the hero survives and the game continues.
The result when a hero reaches zero, including pending healing and other effects.
answers.answer: At zero health, the sidekick is defeated and its token is immediately removed. Its played card still resolves its after-combat effect if the game has not ended. If a hero reaches zero, that player immediately loses and the game ends; do not continue pending effects to heal the hero or finish the turn.

evidence.text: There is no points score. Any fighter reduced to **zero health for any reason is defeated**. Immediately remove a defeated sidekick token. A Harpy is defeated by any damage because it has 1 health.
**A defeated hero immediately loses the duel, and the game ends at once.** Do not continue pending effects to heal that hero or finish the turn. Defeating a sidekick alone does not win the game.
4. Resolve **AFTER COMBAT card effects**. A defeated fighter’s played card still resolves its after-combat effects **unless the game has already ended**.

clauses: How a scheme is played, how the active fighter is declared and selected, and how it resolves and is discarded.
Whether a scheme whose listed fighters are defeated may be played; when a sidekick can be active.
Who may inspect which discard piles and when.
answers.answer: Play a scheme face up from hand, declare an active fighter permitted by its fighter label, resolve its effect, then discard it. You cannot play it if its listed fighters are defeated; a sidekick may be active when the label permits, and ANY permits any surviving fighter. Both players may inspect either discard pile at any time.

evidence.text: Play a scheme (yellow lightning icon) from hand **face up**, declaring a fighter allowed by its fighter label as the **active fighter**. You cannot play a scheme if its listed fighters are defeated. Resolve its effect, then put it in your discard pile.

**A sidekick can be the active fighter for a scheme if the card’s fighter label permits it. ANY permits any of your surviving fighters, hero or sidekick.** Execute the effect for the fighters and destinations it names; being named as a destination or beneficiary does not by itself make that fighter the required initiator.
- Played and resolved cards and discarded cards go into your own **face-up discard pile**, distinct from the face-down deck. Both players may inspect either discard pile **at any time**.

**Alice:** choose BIG or SMALL when placing her at setup. When **BIG**, add **2 to Alice’s attack-card values**. When **SMALL**, add **1 to Alice’s defense-card values**. clauses: Arthur and Merlin’s starting health, attack types and maneuver move value.
When and how Arthur may BOOST an attack through his ability.
What happens to this ability BOOST if the opponent cancels the effects on Arthur’s attack card.
answers.answer: The attached operative text answers the stat lookup. When Arthur attacks, he may play a hand card face down alongside his attack card and add its BOOST value, ignoring its effects; discard the BOOST card. If the opponent cancels the effects on Arthur’s attack card, his ability BOOST is discarded without effect.

The move value applies to **each** of that player’s fighters during maneuver. Harpies have no health dials; each has 1 health. Other fighters have individual dials. Health cannot increase above the highest number on that fighter’s dial.

**King Arthur:** Arthur and Merlin each use **move 2** during maneuver, before any BOOST. When **Arthur attacks**, he may BOOST the attack by playing a hand card **face down alongside his attack card**. Add that card’s BOOST value, ignoring its effects; the BOOST card is discarded. If the opponent **cancels the effects on Arthur’s attack card**, this ability’s BOOST is **discarded without effect**. **Excalibur exception (official 2025 erratum):** Excalibur has no printed effects to cancel, so Feint does not remove the ability BOOST from a textless Excalibur attack. The BOOST still increases its attack value; the ordinary final discard of played cards still applies. See the sourced FAQ below. This is Arthur’s ability, not Merlin’s. **Noble Sacrifice** separately permits another BOOST during combat, in addition to the ability’s BOOST, if its effect is not canceled.
